output.summary: The September 15-16, 2026 minutes lean hawkish for the next (Oct 28) decision. On policy, 'many' favored a higher path on risk-management grounds, 'a number' saw it as necessary on their modal outlook, 'several' judged policy not restrictive, and 'most' expected another year-end increase. Participants stressed decisions remain data-dependent. Net tilt +6 bp (hawkish). All quotes are from the single item fed.minutes.2026-09-16; no watch-outs were specified.

output.summary: The September 15-16, 2026 minutes read decisively hawkish. Participants noted inflation "remained elevated and that they had not seen sufficient progress," several flagged elevated core services ex-housing and short-term inflation expectations, and "Participants generally assessed inflation risk as skewed to the upside," with some seeing those risks "more skewed to the upside in recent months." On labor, conditions were viewed as stable and "close to maximum employment," with a majority seeing recent strengthening and labor-market risks "broadly balanced"; only some participants offered a dovish note that wage growth was "moderate and consistent with inflation moving toward 2 percent." On policy, all participants backed the quarter-point hike to 3-3/4 to 4 percent, "most participants" expected "another increase...would likely be appropriate by year end," many favored a higher path on risk-management grounds, and several saw the rate as "not restrictive or only mildly restrictive." What would change minds: participants emphasized an "open mind" with future decisions depending on "incoming information and its implications for the outlook and the balance of risks." With the next decision on 2026-10-28 and most participants anticipating a further year-end increase, the net lean is clearly hawkish; the tilt is held at +7 rather than the maximum because of the explicit data-dependence caveat and a few dovish/neutral observations.

output.summary: The minutes lean clearly hawkish. On inflation, several participants saw elevated core services and core goods price increases, some judged underlying inflation above 2 percent and moving sideways, several flagged elevated short-term inflation expectations, and many cited rising cost pressures; nearly all saw inflation risks tilted to the upside, with several citing tariffs as upside risk and some worried about expectations becoming entrenched. A lone dovish inflation note came from a few participants citing a material decline in the 3-month core PCE measure. On the labour market, a majority assessed it had strengthened a bit, though several noted unusually low dynamism and some said wages were moderate and not a source of inflation pressure; risks were seen as broadly balanced. On the policy path, many viewed a higher path as prudent risk management, a number saw it as necessary on their modal outlooks, several judged policy not restrictive or only mildly so, and most expected another increase by year end. What would change their minds: future decisions depend on incoming information and the balance of risks. The dominant hawkish quantifiers (majority/almost all/most/many/several favouring firmer policy) against few/some dovish caveats yield a net hawkish tilt of +6 bp for the next decision.

output.summary: The September 15-16, 2026 minutes lean distinctly hawkish. On inflation, multiple quantifier groups flagged elevated core services and core goods inflation, underlying inflation above 2 percent, elevated short-term inflation expectations, increased cost pressures from business contacts, and upside risks from energy, tariffs, and AI demand; only a few/some participants cited dovish offsets (BEA methodology effects, a volatile 3-month core measure, and moderate aggregate wage growth). On the labor market, a majority saw it strengthening a bit and near maximum employment, with risks viewed as broadly balanced, while several noted unusually low dynamism. On policy, all supported the 25bp hike to 3-3/4 to 4 percent, many framed a higher path as prudent risk-management insurance, a number saw it as necessary on their modal outlook, several viewed the rate as not or only mildly restrictive, and most assessed another increase would likely be appropriate by year end. Participants said future decisions would depend on incoming information and the balance of risks, and some noted the trigger of inflation expectations potentially de-anchoring after five years above target. Net tilt is hawkish for the October 28 decision (+6). Watch-outs: none specified.
